title: boxcar audit record v1
description: One line of a session's audit log: a Record, whose `data` is shaped by its `type` as Payload lists (`type` and `data` side by side). See docs/audit-events.md.

ArtifactRef.description: A file the VMM loaded, identified by where it was and what it held.

Attrib.description: Whose identity a record carries as its `subject`.

oneOf.description: The process that made the request.
The process that opened the handle, when the request itself has no usable caller (pid 0, or a write-back from the page cache).

Checkpoint.description: `checkpoint`: a summary the log writer chains in periodically, so a reader can check a stretch of the log against one hash.

dropped.description: Droppable events that were dropped because the audit channel was full.

records_since.description: Records written since the previous checkpoint.

root_hash.description: blake3 over the raw hashes of the records since the previous checkpoint.

ClockSync.description: `sync`: a pairing of the guest's clock with the host's. The VMM pings init over the control channel and times the pong: the guest's `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` when it answered, against the host's at the round trip's midpoint. `ts_host_ns` stays the one timestamp that joins events across rings; this says how far the guest's clock stands from the host's, and how surely.

guest_mono_ns.description: The guest's `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` when it answered, in nanoseconds.

host_mono_ns.description: The host's `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` at the round trip's midpoint.

rtt_ns.description: The round trip, in nanoseconds: the pairing is no surer than this.

ControlConnect.description: `control.connect`: a process connected to the control socket. It is served (`allow`) only when its uid is the VMM's; otherwise the connection is closed before the hello (`deny`).

pid.description: The peer's process id and user id, from `SO_PEERCRED`.

ControlStop.description: `control.stop`: a control client asked the VM to stop.

Evidence.description: A record a finding rests on.

Finding.description: `finding`: the reconciler's conclusion from records of both rings, with the records it read as evidence. Never sampled; a score of 70 or more is written through to disk at once.

evidence.description: The records the rule read, newest last.

low_confidence.description: Whether a join or clock the rule relied on was weak: the score was lowered for it.

rule.description: The rule that fired, by name (see docs/reconciler.md).

score.description: 0 to 100: how strongly the evidence says the agent hid something.

span_id.description: The span the finding belongs to (M4).

summary.description: What was seen, in words; at most 512 bytes.

FindingCategory.description: The kinds of finding; see the design's section 7.

open_seq.description: The `seq` of the record that opened this handle, when known.

path_at_open.description: The path when the handle was opened; differs after a rename.

path_b64.description: `path` as base64 of its raw bytes, set when the name was not valid UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form, `U+FFFD` for each bad byte); omitted otherwise.

size.description: The file size at close, when it was measured.

ts_release_ns.description: Host `CLOCK_REALTIME`, nanoseconds since the epoch, when the guest released the handle: the producer's time, before the hash that completes the record, which can come a while later. 0 in logs written before it existed.

path_b64.description: `path` as base64 of its raw bytes, set when the name was not valid UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form, `U+FFFD` for each bad byte); omitted otherwise.

FsDenied.description: `fs.denied`: an operation was refused for lack of permission.

op.description: The refused operation: `lookup`, `access`, `open`, and so on.

path_b64.description: `path` as base64 of its raw bytes, set when the name was not valid UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form, `U+FFFD` for each bad byte); omitted otherwise.
`path` as base64 of its raw bytes, set when the name was not valid UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form, `U+FFFD` for each bad byte); omitted otherwise.

attrib.description: Whose identity the record's `subject` is: the caller's, or the handle opener's when the request had no usable caller (pid 0, or a write-back from the page cache).

path_b64.description: `path` as base64 of its raw bytes, set when the name was not valid UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form, `U+FFFD` for each bad byte); omitted otherwise.

FsLink.description: `fs.link`: `path` is the new name and `target_path` the file it links to.

path_b64.description: `path` as base64 of its raw bytes, set when the name was not valid UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form, `U+FFFD` for each bad byte); omitted otherwise.
`path` as base64 of its raw bytes, set when the name was not valid UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form, `U+FFFD` for each bad byte); omitted otherwise.
`path` as base64 of its raw bytes, set when the name was not valid UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form, `U+FFFD` for each bad byte); omitted otherwise.

mount.description: The share's tag, such as `root` or `workspace`.

flags_decoded.description: Names of the flags set in `flags`, such as `O_RDWR` and `O_CREAT`.

path_b64.description: `path` as base64 of its raw bytes, set when the name was not valid UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form, `U+FFFD` for each bad byte); omitted otherwise.

FsPathOp.description: `fs.unlink`, `fs.rmdir`, and `fs.readdir`: an operation on one path.

path_b64.description: `path` as base64 of its raw bytes, set when the name was not valid UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form, `U+FFFD` for each bad byte); omitted otherwise.
`path` as base64 of its raw bytes, set when the name was not valid UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form, `U+FFFD` for each bad byte); omitted otherwise.

FsSymlink.description: `fs.symlink`: `path` is the new link and `target` what it points to.

path_b64.description: `path` as base64 of its raw bytes, set when the name was not valid UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form, `U+FFFD` for each bad byte); omitted otherwise.

FsXattr.description: `fs.xattr`: an extended attribute was set or removed.

path_b64.description: `path` as base64 of its raw bytes, set when the name was not valid UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form, `U+FFFD` for each bad byte); omitted otherwise.

Hash.description: A blake3 digest: `b3:` followed by 64 lowercase hex digits.

HashStatus.description: Whether the content of a closed file was hashed, and if not, why.

oneOf.description: The file changed while it was being hashed.
Nothing was written through the handle, so there is nothing to hash.

HttpRequest.description: `http.request`: a request an inspected flow carried, once its body ended. Headers that carry a credential never reach the observer's records: their values are dropped at the parser.

body_b3.description: `b3:` and blake3 of the decoded body; `null` for an empty one.

body_truncated.description: The body passed what the observer keeps (16 MiB): hashed, not read by the model parsers.

degraded.description: Why the request could not be read whole, if it could not: `lost`, `incomplete`, `flow_closed`, `content_encoding`, `content_decode`, a parser's reason.

path.description: The request target, cut at 4096 bytes.

stream.description: HTTP/2's stream id, or 1, 2, 3... for HTTP/1.1's requests in order.

HttpResponse.description: `http.response`: the response to an `http.request`, once it ended; for a WebSocket stream, when it closed.

dur_ms.description: From the request's first byte to the response's last, as the observer took them.

ws_messages.description: Messages of a WebSocket stream, both ways.

LlmRequest.description: `llm.request`: a request to a model API the gate knows, read from an inspected flow once its body ended.

body_bytes.description: Decoded body bytes, and their hash, as the `http.request` has them.

degraded.description: Why the body could not be read: `body_truncated`, `request_json`, or what degraded the `http.request`.

flow.description: The `flow` and `stream` of the `http.request` it was read from.

messages.description: How many messages (or input items) the request carried.

streaming.description: The request asked for a streamed response.

system_b3.description: `b3:` and blake3 of the system prompt (or instructions), if any.

tools.description: The tools offered, by name, at most 64.

LlmResponse.description: `llm.response`: the model's reply to an `llm.request`, once it ended.

degraded.description: Why the reply could not be read whole: `stream_error`, `stream_unfinished`, `block_unfinished`, `call_unfinished`, `event_json`, `response_json`, `body_truncated`, `flow_closed`.

dur_ms.description: From the request's first byte to the reply's last.

stop_reason.description: The provider's stop or finish reason, or status.

text_bytes.description: The assistant's text, by size and blake3 (`b3:`), never inline.

tool_uses.description: How many tool calls the reply made (each a `tool.open`).

dur_ms.description: How long the flow lasted, in milliseconds.

reason.description: Why it ended, such as `fin`, `rst`, `timeout`, `evicted` or `idle`.

NetConnect.description: `net.connect`: a guest connection attempt and the policy's verdict on it.

dst.description: The address and port the guest asked for.

flow.description: The flow's id, unique within the session. The flow's `net.tls` and `net.close` carry it too.

names.description: The names the guest's DNS answers gave `dst`'s address, newest first.

rule.description: The policy rule that decided, as written; `null` when the policy's default did.

src.description: The guest's address and source port.

NetDhcp.description: `net.dhcp`: the network stack answered a guest DHCP message with the session's static lease.

op.description: `offer`, the answer to a DISCOVER, or `ack`, the answer to a REQUEST.

yiaddr.description: The address the reply leases to the guest.

NetDns.description: `net.dns`: a guest DNS query, the policy's verdict on its name, and the answer the guest got.

answers.description: The addresses the answer gave, as text.

qtype.description: The query type, by its DNS number: 1 is A, 28 is AAAA.

rcode.description: The response code the guest got, by its DNS number: 0 is NOERROR, 2 SERVFAIL, 3 NXDOMAIN.

rule.description: The policy rule that decided, as written; `null` when the policy's default did.

txid.description: The transaction id the guest gave the query.

NetDrop.description: `net.drop`: the network stack dropped guest frames. Made at most once a second for each reason, counting every drop since the last.

count.description: Frames dropped for this reason since the last `net.drop` for it.

NetInspect.description: `net.inspect`: the gate ended an inspected flow's TLS, or could not. On `ok`, the record precedes every byte of plaintext relayed; on anything else, nothing was relayed and the flow's `net.close` says `inspect`.

alpn.description: The application protocol both legs agreed on (`h2`, `http/1.1`), or `null` for none or on failure.

result.description: `ok`; `upstream_untrusted` (the real host's certificate is not one the host's store vouches for); `upstream_failed` (its handshake failed otherwise); `guest_rejected` (the guest refused the leaf, or closed during the handshake); `timeout` (the handshakes outran the gate's time).

rule.description: The `inspect` line that named the flow, as written.

sni.description: The server name the guest asked for, or `null` for a flow to an address (a network `inspect` line).

version.description: The TLS version the guest leg speaks (`1.3`, `1.2`), or `null` on failure.

NetTls.description: `net.tls`: the gate's reading of a flow's first bytes, the name they asked for, and whether the flow was let through on it. The gate reads the flows a domain rule allowed: a TLS ClientHello's server name, or a plain HTTP request's `Host`.

alpn.description: The ALPN protocols the ClientHello offered, in its order; empty for `http`.

inspect.description: Whether the policy's `inspect` lines name this flow, so the gate ends its TLS (a `net.inspect` follows) or, for plain HTTP, observes it as it is. Omitted when false.

kind.description: What the first bytes were read as: `tls` (a ClientHello, bytes that began like one, or none at all) or `http` (anything else, read as a plain HTTP request).

sni.description: The name asked for: for `tls`, the server name the ClientHello named; for `http`, the request's `Host` (lowercase, without its port). `null` when there was none to read.

NetUdp.description: `net.udp`: the first datagram of a guest UDP flow, and the policy's verdict on it.

dst.description: The address and port the guest sent to.

flow.description: The flow's id, unique within the session (TCP and UDP flows share one count); its `net.close` carries it.

names.description: The names the guest's DNS answers gave `dst`'s address, newest first.

rule.description: The policy rule that decided, as written; `null` when the policy's default did.

src.description: The guest's address and source port.

OpResult.description: How one operation ended. Present on every filesystem event that performs an operation, so readers can filter failures without knowing the event.

err.description: The symbolic name of `errno`, such as `EACCES`, when Linux defines one.

errno.description: The Linux errno of a failure.

Payload.description:
The typed payloads: one variant per event kind this crate defines.

Adjacently tagged, so it serializes as `{"type": "fs.open", "data": {...}}`, which are the two fields a [`Record`] carries at its top level. New kinds are additive, and a consumer ignores kinds it does not know.

PolicyChanged.description: `policy.changed`: a control client replaced the session's policy (the control socket's `policy.update`): the network rules, the vsock allowlist, or both. The new policy decides every later query, connection and datagram, and what was open and it denies is closed (`net.close{reason:"policy"}`).

version.description: The policy's version from now on: 1 is the policy the VM started with, and each update adds one. `policy.get` reports it.

ProcConnectAttempt.description: `proc.connect_attempt`: a process asked to connect a socket (the LSM's `socket_connect`), with the destination as it asked for it. `dst` and `dst_port` are set for IPv4 and IPv6; another family carries only its number.

family.description: The address family, as `AF_INET` is 2 and `AF_INET6` 10.

proto.description: The socket's transport, such as `tcp` or `udp`.

ProcExec.description: `proc.exec`: a process in the session ran a new program, reported by the sensor after a successful `execve`. The `subject` is the thread that called it, which is the process's leader from then on.

argv.description: The arguments, at most 256 and 16 KiB in all.

cgroup_id.description: The cgroup the process is in: the session's.

filename.description: The program, as the kernel resolved it.

start_ns.description: The process's start time on the guest's clock: with `tgid`, the process's identity across pid reuse.

tid.description: The calling thread's id and its process's.

ProcExit.description: `proc.exit`: a thread in the session ended. `group_dead` when it was the last of its process.

exit_code.description: The kernel's exit code word: the status `wait` reports, signal included.

start_ns.description: The process's start time, as `proc.exec` and `proc.fork` gave it.

ProcFileOpen.description: `proc.file_open`: one open in `sample`, with the path the kernel resolved. The only sampled record of ring 1.

sample.description: The sampling: this record stands for `sample` opens.

ProcFork.description: `proc.fork`: a process in the session made a new process, or a new thread (`thread`): the reconciler needs both, since the filesystem records name the thread that acted.

child_pid.description: The new process's id (its leader thread's, the same), or the new thread's id.

child_start_ns.description: The new task's start time on the guest's clock.

thread.description: Whether the new task is a thread of the parent's process rather than a process of its own.

ProcHeartbeat.description: `proc.heartbeat`: the sensor is alive, once a second. The counters are since it started.

events_emitted.description: Events the sensor took from the kernel's ring buffer.

frames_sent.description: Frames written to the stream, heartbeats included.

ringbuf_drops.description: Events the kernel could not place in the ring buffer: lost.

uptime_ns.description: Since the sensor started, on the guest's clock.

ProcLsmDeny.description: `proc.lsm_deny`: the sensor's self-protection refused something. `hook` is `bpf` (a `bpf()` call by a process other than the sensor, `detail` its command number) or `task_kill` (a signal to the sensor, `detail` the signal number).

ProcMemfd.description: `proc.memfd`: a process made an anonymous memory file (`memfd_create`): a place to hold or run bytes the audited filesystem never sees.

name.description: The name given, at most 256 bytes.

ProcSensorStatus.description: `proc.sensor_status`: what the sensor could attach, sent once it has tried, and again if that changes.

btf_ok.description: Whether the kernel offers its BTF (`/sys/kernel/btf/vmlinux`).

pid.description: The sensor's own process id in the guest, which the guards protect.

programs.description: Every program the sensor carries, attached or not.

reason.description: Why the sensor is degraded, when a single reason covers it (such as `no_programs`).

session_cgroup_id.description: The session cgroup the sensor filters on.

threads.description: The sensor's other threads (the one that reads programs for their TLS symbols): their reads of the shares are the sensor's, not the session's. Absent when it has none.

ProcTcpConnect.description: `proc.tcp_connect`: the kernel sent a connection's first segment: the full 4-tuple once the source port was chosen, which is what joins the flow ring 0 relays (`net.connect`) to the process.

ProcTlsAttach.description: `proc.tls_attach`: the sensor tried to attach its TLS probes to a file: each program the session ran and each `libssl.so*` a session process mapped, once each; `error` is `limit` once after 64 paths. The sensor's own record: no `subject`.

ProcTlsIo.description: `proc.tls_io`: a process wrote to or read from a TLS connection through a runtime that exports OpenSSL's `SSL_write` and `SSL_read` (or their `_ex` forms), which the sensor probed: the size and the time, never the bytes. What names the process behind a model request.

Record.description:
One audit record: one line of a session's log.

The JSON field names are these field names, except that `kind` is `type`. Unset optional fields are left out of the JSON, never written as `null`.

data.description: The payload. Its shape is decided by `kind`; see [`Payload`] for the kinds this crate defines.

prev.description: The `hash` of the previous record, or `genesis_prev` for the first.

seq.description: The record's position in the session, counting from 1 with no gaps. Only the log writer assigns it.

subject.description: The guest process the event is attributed to.

ts_guest_ns.description: The guest's own clock, for events reported from inside the guest. It orders ring 1 events among themselves.

ts_host_ns.description: Host wall-clock time (`CLOCK_REALTIME`) in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, taken when the writer received the event. This is the only timestamp that joins events across rings.

ts_mono_ns.description: Host `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` in nanoseconds, taken at the same moment.

type.description: The dotted event type, such as `fs.open`.

Ring.description: Which side of the VM boundary made the record: 0 the host, 1 the guest.

SensorPhase.description: How much of the sensor runs.

oneOf.description: Some program is not; `programs` says which, and the reconciler skips the rules that need it.

SessionExit.description: `session.exit`: the session's process ended, as init reported it: its exit code, or the signal that killed it. Both are `null` only when init could not tell.

SessionId.description: A session id: a UUIDv7 in lowercase hyphenated text.

SessionStart.description: `session.start`: the guest's init started the session the VMM's config asked for. Reported by init (ring 1); the record's subject is the session's process.

argv.description: The command, as the config gave it.

pid.description: Its process id in the guest.

SetAttr.description: The attributes a `setattr` asked to change. Unset fields were not part of the request and are omitted from the JSON.

ShareRef.description: A directory the VM was given over virtio-fs.

tag.description: The share's tag, such as `root` or `workspace`.

Source.description: The component that produced a record. On the wire, the lowercase name.

oneOf.description: The guest's session, as its init reports it over the control channel.
The session's policy, as the control socket changes it.

SpanEffects.description: `span.effects`: what a tool span held when it closed, or when the VM stopped with it still open: the processes the reconciler attributed to it and the records of their effects. A membership record: the effects themselves are never edited.

closed_seq.description: The seq of the `tool.close`; `null` for a span still open at `vmm.stop`.

effects.description: The seqs of the records attributed to the span, ascending: the `proc.exec` of each process, and the `fs.*` and `net.connect` records their work made; at most 4096.

executor_tgid.description: The process that made the model request the span came from: the one a `proc.tls_io` write named, else the session's root process; `null` when neither is known.

procs.description: The processes attributed to the span, by tgid, in join order; at most 1024.

span_id.description: The provider's tool use id, the span's id in every record's `span`.

truncated.description: Whether a process or an effect was left out for the limits.

SpanRef.description: Where an event sits in a trace.

oneOf.description: Ask the guest to end its session first.

Subject.description: The guest identity an event is attributed to.

ToolClose.description: `tool.close`: the agent sent the tool's result back to the model, in its next request.

result_bytes.description: The result's text, by size and blake3 (`b3:`).

result_summary.description: The result in at most 512 bytes, scrubbed.

status.description: `ok`, or `error` when the agent said so.

ToolOpen.description: `tool.open`: the model asked for a tool to run. Opens the span the record's envelope names (`trace_id` the session, `span_id` the tool use id); the `tool.close` with the same id closes it.

args.description: The arguments, when their JSON is at most 8 KiB; omitted otherwise.

args_b3.description: `b3:` and blake3 of the arguments' JSON.

args_summary.description: The arguments in at most 512 bytes, scrubbed.

tool_use_id.description: The provider's id for the call (`toolu_...`, `call_...`).

VmmStart.description: `vmm.start`: the VM was built and is about to run.

inspect_ca_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the session CA's certificate (DER), lowercase hex, when the session's policy has an `inspect` rule: the authority the guest was told to trust for the gate's certificates. Omitted when the session has none.

shares.description: The virtio-fs shares, in slot order. Omitted when there are none, and read as none when absent.

console_dropped_bytes.description: Console bytes the guest wrote that the host never wrote out: the oldest bytes the console's ring dropped when the host's stdout (or the console file) fell behind, bytes a failed write lost, and what was still undelivered when the stop sequence gave up waiting for a stalled writer. 0 when the console kept up. Absent in logs written before it existed, and read as 0.

stdin_dropped_bytes.description: Bytes typed at the console that the host dropped because the guest was not reading them: the oldest input beyond what the serial FIFO and the host's 4 KiB holding buffer could take. 0 for a run with no console input. Absent in logs written before it existed, and read as 0.

VsockClose.description: `vsock.close`: a vsock connection that a `vsock.connect` let through ended.

VsockConnect.description:
`vsock.connect`: a vsock connection between the guest and the host, and whether it was let through.

A guest connection to an internal port (1024, 1025, 1026) is served by the VMM only from a guest source port below 1024, and only the first such connection to each port; a guest connection to any other port reaches the host socket `<uds>_<port>` only when the port is allowlisted. A host connection, through the vsock socket, is recorded once the guest accepts it.

peer.description: The other end: for a guest connection, `internal` (a VMM service) or `uds` (the host socket `<uds>_<port>`); for a host connection, `guest`.

port.description: The port connected to: the host port for a guest connection, the guest port for a host one.

reason.description: Why a connection was refused: `unprivileged` (an internal port from a guest source port of 1024 or more), `duplicate` (an internal port that was already connected), `no_service` (an internal port nothing serves), `port` (a port that is not allowlisted), or the reason the service at an internal port gave, such as `reactivated` (the guest control channel takes one connection in the VMM's life, and this is a later one, after the guest re-activated its vsock driver). `null` when it was let through.

src_port.description: The connecting side's port: the guest's source port, or the port the VMM gave a host connection.
